applicabilityBasis.summary: ftUSD is a non-yielding dollar-targeted base token marketed for payments and onchain settlement. Product documentation describes conversion into supported collateral assets at a quoted prevailing rate, while the interface terms disclaim Company involvement in underlying protocol transactions. The opened sources do not establish a legal issuer obligation to redeem ftUSD for a fixed amount of national-currency monetary value; that statutory element remains unresolved.

genius.notes: Reviewed on 2026-10-07. ftUSD is a non-yielding dollar-targeted payment and settlement base, distinct from sftUSD and ssftUSD savings receipts. Conversion at a prevailing collateral rate and interface-provider disclaimers do not establish a legal issuer obligation to redeem for fixed national-currency monetary value, so applicability remains unclear. Flying Tulip Ltd is retained verbatim from the current issuerEntity field, but the independently reopened terms identify it only as the interface provider; the legal ftUSD issuer remains unresolved. Separate FT token-sale terms name Flying Tulip FT (BVI) Ltd, while the privacy policy names Flying Tulip (BVI) Ltd. Neither document establishes that those entities issue ftUSD, and no issuerEntity migration is inferred. The public API supplies quantified collateral, supply and strategy disclosures; that first-party report is not independent monthly reserve assurance. Treasury's proposed rule gives January 18, 2027 expected Act effectiveness and July 18, 2028 as the general DASP restriction date. No stronger authorization or foreign exception is claimed.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: As of 2026-10-07, the independently opened regulator implementation materials, Federal Register inventory, NYDFS tables, token disclosures and regulator-domain searches did not identify a qualifying public GENIUS approval, state qualification, named official application, registered foreign exception or GENIUS enforcement action for ftUSD or the Flying Tulip entities reviewed. The current terms establish an interface provider, not a confirmed legal ftUSD issuer. This is a bounded negative-evidence finding and does not establish the absence of confidential or unindexed filings. Ordinary licenses and proposed rules do not establish token-specific GENIUS authorization.
